title: Human-like fleeting memory improves language learning but impairs reading time prediction in transformer language models
abstract: arXiv:2508.05803v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Human memory is fleeting. As words are processed, the exact wordforms that make up incoming sentences are rapidly lost. Cognitive scientists have long believed that this limitation of memory may, paradoxically, help in learning language - an idea supported by classic connectionist modelling work. The rise of Transformers appears to challenge this idea, as these models can learn language effectively, despite lacking memory limitations or other architectural recency biases. translated_title: 类人瞬时记忆提升语言学习但损害Transformer语言模型中的阅读时间预测
translated_abstract: 人类记忆是短暂的。随着单词被处理，构成输入句子的确切词形会迅速丢失。认知科学家长期以来认为，这种记忆限制可能反而有助于语言学习——这一观点得到了经典联结主义建模工作的支持。Transformer的兴起似乎挑战了这一观点，因为这些模型即使没有记忆限制或其他架构上的近因偏差，也能有效学习语言。在此，我们在严格控制的对Transformer语言模型的实验中，研究了瞬时记忆对语言学习的假设性益处。在符合发展现实的训练集上，分别训练有无瞬时记忆的Transformer，我们发现瞬时记忆一致性地改善了语言学习（通过整体语言建模性能和目标句法评估来衡量），但出乎意料的是，它损害了基于惊奇度的预测。
tldr: 瞬时记忆在Transformer语言模型中提升了语言学习能力，但降低了阅读时间预测的准确性。
en_tdlr: Fleeting memory enhances language learning in transformer language models but impairs reading time prediction accuracy.
